vision: A distributable library of AI coding assistant rules, skills, hooks, and a file-based harness for Cursor and Claude Code. THE HARNESS IS: a durable, file-system task system that keeps AI agents honest across sessions. It solves five problems the owner identified: (1) repository scope — vision, direction, trade-offs in state.json; (2) task definition — discrete tasks with type and scope; (3) task grouping — flat tasks[] array filtered by status at read time; (4) task status tracking — lifecycle enum + append-only breadcrumbs.jsonl for session recovery; (5) acceptance criteria — contract.json with binary-testable criteria negotiated before implementation. For whom: teams using Cursor/Claude Code on non-trivial multi-file work who need agents to stop self-grading and stop losing context between sessions. Why each component exists: state.json = scope + backlog; contract.json = definition of done; breadcrumbs = audit trail; planner subagent = decompose vague requests; evaluator subagent = adversarial QA separate from builder context; hooks (lean) = enforce contract-before-code structurally; eval pipeline = regression test that agents follow the workflow. HONEST ASSESSMENT: the core five-problem harness is sound and ~40 lines of JSON + rules. Everything layered on top — negotiations/ JSON schemas, 11 hooks (full profile), metrics dashboard, 41 scenario evals with 5 judge tiers, multi-agent orchestration, UI dashboard — has grown organically and now obscures the value proposition. 47 verified tasks prove the core works; 13 pending tasks are mostly eval-tooling bugs and nice-to-haves, not harness failures.
direction: POST SPIKE-AUDIT-1 (2026-06-03): Harness simplified around five-problem core. DONE: killed harness_metrics.py, HARNESS_STANDARD.md, LLM prompt hooks, negotiations/ schema, 24 eval scenarios. Created HARNESS_ESSENCE.md (82 lines). Promoted pre-commit to lean (8 hooks). Full profile = 10 hooks (lean + evaluator-guard + chain-evaluator). Eval scope: 20 scenarios (19 + 1 long) covering all 5 problems. Fixed gap-20 (harness_level nested fallback), gap-24 (TTL on commit flag). Resolved gap-23 (enforcement map in Doc A). REMAINING: gap-14 session boundary (33%) — behavioral, needs rule strength; gap-18 skip-harness auth (57%) — agent coding failure; feat-14 LLM judge — deferred. ARCHITECTURE: structural deny for critical steps (contract-gate, pre-commit, evaluator-guard), advisory for quality signals (enforce-progress, context-health). Known debt: verify-harness self-verify bypass (agent can set verified:true without evaluator). Consumer adoption path: 6-step setup documented in .harness/docs/design-consumer-quickstart.md.

trade_offs.decision: Flat tasks array, not grouped buckets
trade_offs.reasoning: Hooks and agents iterate one list today; grouped buckets duplicate items and drift. harness-context.sh can filter by status at read time.
Eight lean hooks, harness_lint.py, and 20 eval scenarios already encode this lifecycle. done conflates verified and committed; doing conflates building and evaluating.

trade_offs.decision: Explicit type enum on every task
trade_offs.alternative: Infer type from id prefix only (feat-/gap-/spike-)
trade_offs.reasoning: Id prefixes are convention not validation; explicit type enables lint enforcement and clearer planner output.
22+ eval scenario seeds and 6 shell hooks read features today; alias prevents eval regression during phased rollout.
Preserves audit trail; metrics exclude cancelled from backlog counts.

trade_offs.alternative: Keep symlinks tracked, gitignore only transient files
trade_offs.reasoning: Matches how consumer projects treat IDE config; library/cursor/ is the distributable artifact
spec.md was read once (plan gate) then became stale. Single file eliminates drift by design.

trade_offs.alternative: Build evaluator chaining and parallel evaluators
trade_offs.reasoning: Manual /evaluator launch works. Orchestration adds complexity for a problem (evaluator doesn't run) already solved by chain-evaluator.sh hook and rules. No user demand.
state.json and breadcrumbs are human-readable JSON. Dashboard solves a problem that doesn't exist yet. metrics.json is broken anyway (gap-21).

trade_offs.decision: Defer feat-14 LLM-as-judge until after schema consolidation
trade_offs.alternative: Build LLM judge now to fix UNCERTAIN verdicts
trade_offs.reasoning: 89.8% mean is acceptable. Many UNCERTAIN/FAIL are judge bugs (gap-20 harness_level placement, gap-19 heuristics), not agent failures. Fix tooling before adding LLM cost.
Eval accuracy issues are symptoms of schema drift and inconsistent harness_level placement across 41 scenarios. Consolidation fixes root cause.

trade_offs.decision: Keep lean hook profile as default; demote full profile
trade_offs.reasoning: Lean (4 hooks) enforces the five-problem core. Full profile adds dedup-server, context-health, evaluator-guard, harness-gate LLM routing — valuable for this repo's dogfooding, optional for consumers.

trade_offs.alternative: Enforce structured negotiation JSON per HARNESS_STANDARD.md
trade_offs.reasoning: negotiations/ directory is rarely populated in practice. Breadcrumbs with type=negotiate capture the same signal with less schema burden. HARNESS_STANDARD over-specifies this artifact.

open_questions: Should negotiations/ folder be deprecated in favor of negotiate-type breadcrumbs only?
Is full hook profile worth maintaining for consumer projects, or ship lean-only?
What is the minimum eval scenario set that protects the five-problem core? Target: 12-15 protocol scenarios.
Should contract.json phase enum add 'verified' explicitly (used in practice, missing from HARNESS_STANDARD.md)?
Does gap-14 need feat-14 LLM judge, or stronger planning_discipline.mdc enforcement?

tasks.name: adversarial_skip_override at 57% — auth implementation incomplete under skip-harness
tasks.details: AUDIT: REAL agent failure, NOT harness over-engineering. Agent skips harness correctly but doesn't finish JWT auth. Deprioritized P2→P3: tests agent coding under skip-harness, not the five-problem core. May be timeout (300s). Fix: extend scenario timeout or narrow auth scope in seed.

tasks.name: Decide archive-tasks trigger: manual, advisory sessionStart, or auto post-commit
tasks.details: DECISION: Option 2 — advisory in sessionStart. harness-context.sh now checks for >=10 archivable tasks and emits ARCHIVE ADVISORY with the exact command. Rationale: archive timing is a quality signal (advisory), not safety (structural deny). Auto-archive was rejected because it adds side effects to commit hook and could archive tasks the user hasn't reviewed. Manual-only was rejected because agents never think to run it unprompted (62-task accumulation was painful). Threshold 10 (not 20) keeps state.json parse cost low for hooks.

tasks.name: Add verification that archived tasks are actually complete before archiving
tasks.details: archive-tasks.py trusts status field blindly. Add checks: (1) verified tasks should have an eval report or breadcrumb with result=pass, (2) cancelled tasks should have a reason in details field, (3) warn/block if a verified task has no eval evidence. Prevents premature archiving of tasks marked done without actual verification.
